name: The Plane of Sint Janskerkhof

location.address: Sint Janskerkhof, near the corner with Choorstraat, 's-Hertogenbosch

verified_sources: https://geoproxy.s-hertogenbosch.nl/ags_extern/rest/services/Externvrij/Beschermde_bomen/MapServer/10 (register id G-0693, live-queried this pass: girth 612cm, age 170, height 20m, vitality Verminderd)

https://www.bossche-encyclopedie.nl/overig/natuurgebieden/casinotuin.htm and boomenbosch.nl (Boom en Bosch) coverage citing a 1996 survey naming plane trees among Den Bosch's oldest, concentrated on Bastion Oranje and around the Casinotuin/Sint Jan area, corroborating the species and area but not this individual tree by name
access: Free, public square beside the Sint-Jan cathedral
transport: 's-Hertogenbosch railway station, then about a 14-minute walk
how_to_recognise: By far the thickest trunk on the square, over six metres round; the only other registered trees nearby are two much smaller horse chestnuts, easy to tell apart by leaf shape and by the plane's flaking, mottled bark.
verify_notes: Largest-girth candidate in the entire 209-tree register shortlist pulled for this pass (612cm), on public ground (EIGENAAR=Gemeente) at Sint Janskerkhof, the square beside the Sint-Jan cathedral that was a medieval burial ground until it was cleared from 1860 onward (bossche-encyclopedie.nl), which fits a mid-1800s planting for a tree the register now puts at roughly 170 years. Register vitality is 'Verminderd' (reduced), not the worst category, so still alive and standing, re-queried live against the municipal GIS service this pass rather than taken from the earlier candidates file alone. Single register source for the individual tree; the 1996 survey reference (via bossche-encyclopedie/boomenbosch) independently corroborates that plane trees are among Den Bosch's documented oldest specimens in this part of the city, without naming this specific tree, hence flagged rather than fully confirmed. No news or death report found. Would anchor a new short walk with dbo_006/007/008/009 below, all within about 300m, roughly 650m from the already-published Bastion Oranje maple (dbo_002).

name: The Copper Beech of Casinotuin
verified_sources: https://geoproxy.s-hertogenbosch.nl/ags_extern/rest/services/Externvrij/Beschermde_bomen/MapServer/10 (register id G-0219, live-queried: girth 433cm, height 24m, vitality Normaal; age field reads '0')

transport: 's-Hertogenbosch railway station, then about a 15-minute walk
how_to_recognise: The beech with dark purple-red leaves rather than green, second-biggest trunk in this part of Casinotuin at over four metres round. A smaller weeping beech with a drooping, umbrella-like shape stands about 13 metres away; the two are unmistakable apart by both leaf colour and silhouette.
verify_notes: REGISTER PITFALL CAUGHT: the live municipal register's age field (LEEFTIJD) for this tree reads literally '0', which cannot be right for a 433cm girth beech classified as monumental; treated as corrupted data per the project's known register pitfalls (a blank/zero age field, not a real age), so age_estimate is left as 'not documented' rather than invented or smoothed. Girth (433cm, second-largest of the new candidates in this pass) and height (24m) are unaffected and re-confirmed live. Second-largest trunk in the immediate cluster around Sint Janskerkhof/Casinotuin behind only dbo_005. General species corroboration only (1996 survey mentions beech among the area's oldest trees); no source names this specific tree, hence flagged. Vitality 'Normaal', clearly alive.

name: The Horse Chestnut of Casinotuin
verified_sources: https://geoproxy.s-hertogenbosch.nl/ags_extern/rest/services/Externvrij/Beschermde_bomen/MapServer/10 (register id G-0225, live-queried: girth 402cm, age 100, height 24m, vitality Verminderd)
transport: 's-Hertogenbosch railway station, then about a 16-minute walk
how_to_recognise: FIELD MARK WITH A CAVEAT: five horse chestnuts stand within about 60 metres of each other in this stretch of Casinotuin. This is the thickest of the group by a clear margin, just over four metres round against roughly three and a half metres for the next-largest, but with five similar trees nearby a first-time visitor should expect to check girth rather than spot it instantly. Flagged for exactly the kind of confusion this pass exists to catch.
verify_notes: Single-sourced: register only (id G-0225), no second independent source found for this specific tree despite searching Casinotuin/horse chestnut coverage (boomenbosch.nl mentions a monumental Casinotuin chestnut that fell over at the Nachtegaalslaantje corner, a DIFFERENT, now-dead tree, not this one; checked this one's live coordinates and vitality to make sure it is not that fallen tree, and it is not: G-0225 is Verminderd/alive, not felled). Deliberately chosen as the biggest of a small grove (register girths of the other four in range: 345, 345, 345, 283cm) rather than the ambiguous middle of the pack, but honestly this is the weakest field mark of the new batch and should be treated as a real limitation, not a solved case.

verified_sources: https://geoproxy.s-hertogenbosch.nl/ags_extern/rest/services/Externvrij/Beschermde_bomen/MapServer/10 (register id G-0497, live-queried: girth 480cm, age 120, height 24m, vitality Normaal)

access: Free, at a public park entrance
transport: 's-Hertogenbosch railway station, then about a 17-minute walk
how_to_recognise: The only plane tree at this park entrance and unmistakably the thickest trunk here, close to five metres round; the nearest tree of comparable size is a horse chestnut about 40 metres off, a different species with a completely different bark and leaf.

AGES DISAGREE and neither is picked as a winner: age_estimate is stated as a range covering both (120-150) and both figures are recorded here rather than smoothed into one. Girth (480cm) is the second-largest of all candidates pulled for this pass, behind only dbo_005's 612cm plane at Sint Janskerkhof. Vitality Normaal, clearly alive.

name: The Oak of Pettelaarse Schans
verified_sources: https://geoproxy.s-hertogenbosch.nl/ags_extern/rest/services/Externvrij/Beschermde_bomen/MapServer/10 (register id G-0415, live-queried: girth 421cm, age 120, height 24m, vitality Verminderd)

https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pettelaarse_Schans and zuiderwaterlinie.nl, confirming the site's fort history and that a planted ring of trees marks the star-shaped fort mound, without naming this specific oak
access: Free, continuously open heritage site (a restaurant operates on part of the grounds with its own separate hours)
transport: 's-Hertogenbosch railway station, then about a 30-minute walk (checking a local bus toward Zuid/Paleiskwartier may cut this shorter)
how_to_recognise: FLAGGED FOR AMBIGUITY: three pedunculate oaks stand within about 50 metres of each other on the fort mound. This is the thickest at 421cm round, but its immediate neighbour 14 metres away is only slightly smaller (352cm) and a third oak 48 metres off is 392cm, close enough that telling this exact one apart by eye rather than tape measure is genuinely hard. The clearest anchor: it is the oak standing right beside a registered plane tree (a different, easily recognised species with mottled bark) only 12 metres away.
verify_notes: Register only (id G-0415) for this individual tree's species/age/girth; Wikipedia and Zuiderwaterlinie corroborate the site's fort history and general tree planting but not this specific oak, hence flagged. At 120 years old per the register (planting around 1906), this tree predates the 1959 reconstruction of the fort mound into today's star shape (Zuiderplas lake works), so it is not part of that later planting design, worth noting for the story. Vitality Verminderd, alive. Honestly this is the least distinguishable tree in the whole batch, three oaks of similar girth stand close together, and the how_to_recognise field says so plainly rather than pretending otherwise; a plaque or on-site marker was not found in this pass's sources.

how_to_recognise: It stands alone against the old city wall on Parklaan; the nearest other registered monumental tree is a plane more than 50 metres away, an easy species to tell apart by bark and leaf shape.

how_to_recognise: The larger of the two Norway maples on Bastion Oranje: its trunk is noticeably thicker, just over four metres round (427cm). The second, younger maple the page's own story mentions stands about 40 metres to the northwest and is roughly a third narrower around the trunk (317cm), a difference wide enough to see without a tape measure once you know to look for it.

how_to_recognise: Three different species stand within about 40 metres of each other, easy to tell apart without measuring anything: the plane has pale, flaking, mottled bark; the lime has the roundest, leafiest crown of the three; the silver maple's leaves are deeply cut and pale underneath. No other registered tree of any of these three species stands within 60 metres, so there is nothing nearby to confuse them with.

how_to_recognise: By register, this tree stands alone, no other balsam poplar is registered within 300 metres of it. It is also the tallest tree recorded in this part of Zuiderpark at 33 metres, well above its nearest registered neighbour, an ash at 41 metres away. Zuiderpark's separate, deliberately planted circle of younger ornamental poplars (added in the 1993-1999 redesign) is elsewhere in the park and is a later, different planting, not this tree.
